On Oct 29, 2028, at 07:25, sean_gallagher@redwood.com wrote:
> Forwarding Clearline ops report. PagerDuty PD-5689 opened.

Initial findings from quick triage:
- svc-gateway-eu LB shows a spike in 502/503 responses originating from upstream pool A (10.2.3.0/24). Backend instances in pool A are returning 504s due to request queue timeouts.
- We see an increase in client retries (exponential retry flood) from several Clearline IP ranges; retries amplify load and push backpressure to origin.
- No recent infra deploys in the last 45m. We rolled a config tweak to the ratelimiter yesterday but on a different cluster (not eu).

Immediate actions taken:
- Increased backend pool capacity for svc-gateway-eu (added 6 warm instances)
- Enabled fallback route (route B) to reduce pressure on pool A
- Temporarily bumped per-ip concurrency limit for Clearline to reduce 429s that were driving retry loops

Next steps:
- Force-drain the most overloaded instances in pool A for a clean reboot
- Monitor 1-minute error rate and user impact; will report back in 10 minutes

Attaching the quick failover runbook we used.

Attachments: runbook_gateway_failover.pdf

— Marissa
Marissa Cole
Sr Engineering Manager, Edge Reliability

Quick executive summary for the record and next steps before the Waveboard: 

What happened:
- A sudden latency amplification at the gateway in eu-west-1 produced a cascade: backend request queueing → 504s → gateway returned 502/503 to clients → client SDKs retried aggressively → amplified burst and elevated 429s + prolonged failure window.

Customer impact:
- Clearline: ~15–25% of checkout attempts failed during the window; revenue-impacting. Multiple enterprise merchants filing support tickets.

Mitigation so far:
- Increased backend capacity + enabled route B fallback
- Temporary per-ip concurrency bump and targeted rate-limiter adjustments for Clearline

Open decisions for execs:
- Offer one-time SLA credit or service credit (recommend 5% for the impacted hour) — need approval
- Approve post-incident deep-dive owner: propose Marissa (lead), Jonas (infra), Grace (observability)
- Approve a short-term conservancy: automatic fallback thresholds lowered to avoid similar amplification (opt-in per-customer)

Quoted from Clearline ops: "This is causing checkout abandonment and customer escalations — please advise ETA."

I'll stand up Waveboard at 08:15 UTC and invite Clearline. Please confirm availability.

Jonas Weber
Director, Production Engineering
